items.prompt: Which admitted line is the bounded future?
items.feedback: Я поговорю три́дцать мину́т is the bounded future example here: its perfective verb presents a limited stretch of speaking, and the line states thirty minutes. Я бу́ду говори́ть uses a future auxiliary and imperfective infinitive without a stated duration in this option. Both refer to the future, not to an event already completed. A stated duration does not automatically require perfective aspect in every sentence.
distractorRationales: Я бу́ду говори́ть is the supplied imperfective future option without the thirty-minute limit stated in the other line; it does not match this bounded future example.

distractorDifference: Я бу́ду говори́ть is the supplied imperfective future option without the thirty-minute limit stated in the other line; it does not match this bounded future example.
assessment.whyAnswerDemonstratesObjective: Я поговорю три́дцать мину́т is the bounded future example here: its perfective verb presents a limited stretch of speaking, and the line states thirty minutes. Я бу́ду говори́ть uses a future auxiliary and imperfective infinitive without a stated duration in this option. Both refer to the future, not to an event already completed. A stated duration does not automatically require perfective aspect in every sentence.

items.prompt: Which admitted line is the bounded future?
items.promptLetter: I will work for three hours
items.feedback: Я порабо́таю три ча́са is the bounded future example here: the perfective verb presents a limited stretch of work, and the line states three hours. Я бу́ду рабо́тать is the supplied auxiliary-plus-imperfective future without that stated duration. The limit describes this work period, not necessarily completion of a task. A definite time period does not by itself force perfective aspect.
distractorRationales: Я бу́ду рабо́тать is the supplied imperfective future option without the three-hour limit stated in the other line; it does not match this bounded future example.

distractorDifference: Я бу́ду рабо́тать is the supplied imperfective future option without the three-hour limit stated in the other line; it does not match this bounded future example.
assessment.whyAnswerDemonstratesObjective: Я порабо́таю три ча́са is the bounded future example here: the perfective verb presents a limited stretch of work, and the line states three hours. Я бу́ду рабо́тать is the supplied auxiliary-plus-imperfective future without that stated duration. The limit describes this work period, not necessarily completion of a task. A definite time period does not by itself force perfective aspect.

items.prompt: Which admitted line is the unbounded future?
items.feedback: Я бу́ду говори́ть is the unbounded future example in this pair: the future auxiliary plus imperfective infinitive presents speaking without a stated duration. Я поговорю три́дцать мину́т presents a limited stretch and states thirty minutes. Unbounded here describes the supplied option; it does not mean the activity lasts forever or that imperfective future can never have a duration.
distractorRationales: Я поговорю три́дцать мину́т is the bounded future option with a stated thirty-minute limit, rather than the unbounded future example requested here.

distractorDifference: Я поговорю три́дцать мину́т is the bounded future option with a stated thirty-minute limit, rather than the unbounded future example requested here.
assessment.whyAnswerDemonstratesObjective: Я бу́ду говори́ть is the unbounded future example in this pair: the future auxiliary plus imperfective infinitive presents speaking without a stated duration. Я поговорю три́дцать мину́т presents a limited stretch and states thirty minutes. Unbounded here describes the supplied option; it does not mean the activity lasts forever or that imperfective future can never have a duration.

items.prompt: Which admitted line is the first-person plural future?
items.feedback: Мы бу́дем говори́ть is first-person plural future: the subject means we, and the future auxiliary agrees with that plural subject. Я бу́ду говори́ть is first-person singular, meaning I. The imperfective infinitive stays the same; the subject and auxiliary distinguish the number requested.
distractorRationales: Я бу́ду говори́ть is first-person singular future, not the first-person plural future requested here.

distractorDifference: Я бу́ду говори́ть is first-person singular future, not the first-person plural future requested here.
assessment.whyAnswerDemonstratesObjective: Мы бу́дем говори́ть is first-person plural future: the subject means we, and the future auxiliary agrees with that plural subject. Я бу́ду говори́ть is first-person singular, meaning I. The imperfective infinitive stays the same; the subject and auxiliary distinguish the number requested.

items.prompt: Which admitted row is the third-person plural future?
items.feedback: ска́жут is the third-person plural future form of this perfective verb, used with they. скажу́ is first-person singular, used with I. The cue shows third-person singular, but the question asks for third-person plural of the same verb. These forms refer to future events, not events already completed.
distractorRationales: скажу́ is first-person singular future, not the requested third-person plural future.

distractorDifference: скажу́ is first-person singular future, not the requested third-person plural future.
assessment.whyAnswerDemonstratesObjective: ска́жут is the third-person plural future form of this perfective verb, used with they. скажу́ is first-person singular, used with I. The cue shows third-person singular, but the question asks for third-person plural of the same verb. These forms refer to future events, not events already completed.

items.prompt: Which admitted line is the first-person singular future?
items.feedback: Я бу́ду говори́ть is first-person singular future: the subject means I, and the auxiliary agrees with one speaker. Мы бу́дем говори́ть is first-person plural, meaning we. Both use the same imperfective infinitive after the future auxiliary; choose singular agreement.
distractorRationales: Мы бу́дем говори́ть is first-person plural future, not the first-person singular future requested here.

distractorDifference: Мы бу́дем говори́ть is first-person plural future, not the first-person singular future requested here.
assessment.whyAnswerDemonstratesObjective: Я бу́ду говори́ть is first-person singular future: the subject means I, and the auxiliary agrees with one speaker. Мы бу́дем говори́ть is first-person plural, meaning we. Both use the same imperfective infinitive after the future auxiliary; choose singular agreement.

items.prompt: Which admitted line is the impersonal past for one person who was cold?
items.feedback: Ему было холодно is the impersonal past example meaning he was cold: the experiencer is dative singular, while the verb is neuter singular. Им было скучно describes plural experiencers who were bored. Both options are impersonal past and keep the same neuter singular verb; the requested person and state distinguish them.
distractorRationales: Им было скучно is also impersonal past, but it describes plural experiencers who were bored, not the singular cold person requested here.

distractorDifference: Им было скучно is also impersonal past, but it describes plural experiencers who were bored, not the singular cold person requested here.
assessment.whyAnswerDemonstratesObjective: Ему было холодно is the impersonal past example meaning he was cold: the experiencer is dative singular, while the verb is neuter singular. Им было скучно describes plural experiencers who were bored. Both options are impersonal past and keep the same neuter singular verb; the requested person and state distinguish them.

items.prompt: Which admitted line is the impersonal past for more than one bored person?
items.feedback: Им было скучно is the impersonal past example meaning they were bored: the experiencers are dative plural, but the verb remains neuter singular. Ему было холодно describes one male experiencer who was cold. Both options are impersonal past; plural experiencers do not turn the verb into a plural form in this construction.
distractorRationales: Ему было холодно is also impersonal past, but it describes one male experiencer who was cold, not the plural bored experiencers requested here.

distractorDifference: Ему было холодно is also impersonal past, but it describes one male experiencer who was cold, not the plural bored experiencers requested here.
assessment.whyAnswerDemonstratesObjective: Им было скучно is the impersonal past example meaning they were bored: the experiencers are dative plural, but the verb remains neuter singular. Ему было холодно describes one male experiencer who was cold. Both options are impersonal past; plural experiencers do not turn the verb into a plural form in this construction.

items.prompt: Which admitted line is the impersonal past for one woman who was cold?
items.feedback: ей было холодно is the impersonal past example meaning she was cold: the experiencer is feminine dative singular, while the verb remains neuter singular. Ему было холодно is the supplied he was cold example with a masculine dative experiencer. Both options are impersonal past; the woman in the question changes the experiencer pronoun, not the verb to feminine agreement.
distractorRationales: Ему было холодно is also impersonal past, but the supplied example refers to a male experiencer, not the woman requested here.

distractorDifference: Ему было холодно is also impersonal past, but the supplied example refers to a male experiencer, not the woman requested here.
assessment.whyAnswerDemonstratesObjective: ей было холодно is the impersonal past example meaning she was cold: the experiencer is feminine dative singular, while the verb remains neuter singular. Ему было холодно is the supplied he was cold example with a masculine dative experiencer. Both options are impersonal past; the woman in the question changes the experiencer pronoun, not the verb to feminine agreement.
